issues.description:
Method: messageOnMilk
Problem statement prose (lines 93-95) instructs a signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and return value including the volume "[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)". However, the UML in the problem statement (lines 51-53), the template usage (Main.java calls m.messageOnMilk() at lines 30-31), and the solution repository declare and implement a no-argument method messageOnMilk(): String (solution Milkable.java interface and Seal/Goat implementations). This is a direct parameter-list mismatch: some artifacts require a double parameter while others use no parameters. A student following the prose will implement a different signature than the template/solution/tests expect, causing compilation errors or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent API and update all artifacts accordingly. Option A (preferred minimal change): keep the no-argument signature messageOnMilk(): String used in the UML, template, and solution — update the problem statement prose (lines ~93) to require messageOnMilk(): String and change the example return format to "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (remove the volume). Option B (if volume tracking is required): change the Milkable interface to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume): String, update all implementations (Seal, Goat, etc.) and all call sites (Main, Farm/tests) to pass a double, and update the UML and prose to match. Ensure tests and provided template code match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The milk-action method's signature is inconsistent across the problem statement and the code. Concept: the method that reports milking an animal (messageOnMilk). Problem statement Part 2 (problem_statement.md line 93) instructs students to implement messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (a method with a double parameter). However, the UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md line 52) and the code artifacts use a no-argument method messageOnMilk(): String. Template Main.java calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 30-31). The solution declares the interface as String messageOnMilk() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5) and implements the no-argument method in Seal (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java lines 19-20) and Goat (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java lines 15-16). A student following the textual Part 2 requirement (double parameter) would implement a different signature than the template and tests expect, causing compilation or test failures and confusion about the correct API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the code to the same method signature. Preferred fix: update the textual Part 2 in problem_statement.md to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and adjust the example return value text to match the no-argument form (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Alternatively, if the intent is to track volume, change the template and solution to declare/implement messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) everywhere (interfaces, implementations, and any calls) and update tests and examples accordingly. The simplest and least disruptive option is to make the problem statement match the existing no-argument signature used in the template and solution.
